Notes: Web_Programming- Html Forms

Html Forms
Forms are one of the most important elements in the HTML tags which is used for creating user interface and accepting input from the user using different types of input controls like text filed, password field, check boxes, radio buttons, drop down boxes etc. We will throw a light on all these features  in this chapter.
Introduction to HTML Forms
Basics of HTML form
  • HTML Forms are required when there is need to collect some data from the site visitor. For example during user registration we would like to collect information such as name, email address, credit card, etc. A form will take input from the site visitor and then will post it to a back-end application.
  • The back-end application will perform required processing on the passed data based on defined business logic inside the application.
  • There are various form elements available like text fields, textarea fields, drop-down menus, radio buttons, checkboxes, etc.
  • The HTML <form> tag is used to create an HTML form.
Basic form element
<form action="process.php" method="post">
      <!-- different input elements  -->
</form>
Form attributes
There are 3 main attributes of form element which are:
  1. action :  This attribute is used to specify backend script ready to process your passed data.
  2. method : This attribute is used to specify method to be used to upload data. The most frequently used are GET and POST methods.
  3. enctype : This is used to specify how the browser encodes the data before it sends it to the server. Possible values are:
    application/x-www-form-urlencoded: This is the standard method most forms use in simple scenarios. mutlipart/form-data: This is used when you want to upload binary data in the form of files like image, word file etc.
Basic formOutput
<form action="process.php" method="post">
    First Name : 
   <input type="text" name="firstname" /> <br/>
   Last Name :
   <input type="text" name="lastname" /> <br/>
  <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
</form>		​
Use of get and post
  • Before the browser sends the information, it encodes it using a scheme called URL encoding. In this scheme, name/value pairs are joined with equal signs and different pairs are separated by the ampersand.     name1=value1&name2=value2&name3=value3
  • The GET method sends the encoded user information appended to the page request. The page and the encoded information are separated by the ? character.   
    http://www.test.com/index.htm?name1=value1&name2=value2
  • The POST method transfers information via HTTP headers. The information is encoded as described in case of GET method and put into a header called QUERY_STRING.
Difference between get and post
Sr NoGETPOST
1The GET method is restricted to send upto 1024 characters only.
The POST method does not have any restriction on data size to be sent.
2GET can't be used to send binary data, like images or word documents, to the server.
The POST method can be used to send ASCII as well as binary data.
3Never use GET method if you have password or other sensitive information to be sent to the server.
It is safe to send sensitive information like password or account numbers using post method
4Get methods can be bookmarked
Post methods can not be bookmarked
5Get is the default method
Post is not the default method

Different Form elements
The <input> Element
The most important form element is the <input> element. The <input> element can be displayed in several ways, depending on the type attribute. For all input types name attribute is very important to write which identify the form element. The value of name attribute is used to send data to the server in key-value pairs. Name attribute is used as key for the data and value is what is entered by user.
Input Type Text   
 <input type="text"> defines a one-line text input field. Most browsers have a default width that allows for displaying around 20-25 characters.
HTMLOutput
<form>
    First name : <br/>
    <input type="text" name="fname"/> <br/>
    Last name : <br/>
    <input type="text" name="lname" /> <br/>
    <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
</form>		​

Input Type Password     
<input type="password"> defines a password field. This type of input field allows users to input sensitive information, such as passwords, which displays characters as asterisks or dots.
HTMLOutput
<form>
    User name : <br/>
    <input type="text" name="username"/> <br/>
    User password : <br/>
    <input type="password" name="psw" /> <br/>
    <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
</form>		​

Input Type Radio
<input type="radio"> defines a radio button. Radio buttons let a user select ONLY ONE of a limited number of choices.
HTMLOutput
<form>
    Select gender :
    <input type="radio" name="gender"
    value="M" checked /> Male
    <input type="radio" name="gender"
    value="F" /> Female  
    <input type="radio" name="gender"
    value="Other" /> Other  <br/>
</form>
<!-- checked attribute is used to specify the radio
button should be displayed as selected -->		​

Input Type Checkbox
<input type="checkbox"> defines a checkbox. Check boxes let a user select ZERO or MORE options of a limited number of choices.
HTMLOutput
<form>
    Select gender :
    <input type="checkbox" name="vehicle1"
    value="bike" checked /> I have a bike
    <input type="checkbox" name="vehicle2"
    value="Car" /> I have a car
</form>
<!-- checked attribute is used to specify the checkbox
should be displayed as selected -->		​

The <select> Element
The <select> element defines a drop-down list. A select box, also called drop down box which provides option to list various options in the form of drop down list, from where a user can select one or more options.
HTMLOutput
<form>
    Select city :
    <select name="city">
       <option value="C01">Pune</option>
       <option value="C03">Mumbai</option>
       <option value="C10">Delhi</option>
       <option value="C12">Chennai</option>
    </select>   <br/>
</form>
<!-- in this select box user can select only one option -->		​
<form>
    Select city :
    <select name="city" size="3" multiple>
       <option value="C01">Pune</option>
       <option value="C03">Mumbai</option>
       <option value="C10">Delhi</option>
       <option value="C12">Chennai</option>
    </select>   <br/>
</form>
<!-- in this select box user can select multiple options and 3 options are displayed at a time as size=3 -->		​
The <textarea> Element
The <textarea> element defines a multi-line input field (a text area). This is used when the user is required to give details that may be longer than a single sentence. Multi-line input controls are created using HTML <textarea> tag.
HTML    Output
<form>
Enter comment : <textarea rows="3" cols="40" name="comment">
    Enter your comment here....
</textarea>   <br/>
</form>		​
Button Element
This element defines a clickable button. There are 3 different types of buttons.
  1. <input type="submit"> : defines a button for submitting form data to a form-handler. The form-handler is typically a server page which processes input data. The form-handler is specified in the form's action attribute
  2. <input type="reset"> : defines a reset button that will reset all form values to their default values
  3. <input type="button"> : defines the button which is used for calling some java script code for performing client side operations.
File upload element
If you want to allow a user to upload a file, a file upload box, also known as a file select box is required. This is also created using the <input> element but type attribute is set to file. 
HTMLOutput
<form>
    Select file to upload :
    <input type="file" name="resume"  />    
</form>		​
Hidden form element
Hidden form controls are used to hide data inside the page which later on can be pushed to the server. This control hides inside the code and does not appear on the actual page. 
HTMLOutput
<form>
    User name : <br/>
    <input type="text" name="username"/> <br/>
    <input type="hidden" name="id" value="AP198" /> <br/>
    <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
    <input type="reset" value="Clear" />
</form>		​
Check here hidden input element is not displayed



Advantages of HTML 5
As the name suggests, HTML5 is the 5th version of HTML (Hypertext Markup Language). HTML5 is the latest specification of the HTML language. HTML5 comes with a variety of new and advanced features that make the life of developers more easy and flexible. There are many features added in HTML 5. We will discuss the important ones :
  1. New semantic elements
  2. Audio and video elements
  3. Canvas element
  4. New input types
  5. Validation attributes
New semantic elements
HTML5 introduced several semantic elements, which are designed to provide more meaningful structure to web pages, so that it is easier to understand for both humans and machines. These elements are not meant for specifying how the content should be styled. But it is used for specifying the purpose or meaning of the content they enclose. Before HTML 5, this was possible to achieve using div tags by giving id attribute. Few semantic elements are :
  1. <header>: Represents introductory content or a group of navigational links at the top of a section or page.
  2. <footer>: Represents footer content or a group of navigational links at the bottom of a section or page.
  3. <nav>: Represents a section of the document that contains navigation links, such as menus or tables of contents.
  4. <article>: Represents a self-contained piece of content that can be distributed and reused independently from the rest of the page, such as a blog post, news article, or forum post.
  5. <section>: Represents grouping of content within a document, such as chapters, headers, footers, or any other content grouped with a common theme.
Advantage : This improves web page readability and understandability for the programmer which helps in easy modification and maintenance.
Audio and video elements
With Audio and Video tags, developers can directly embed videos or audio files into the web pages. 
HTMLOutput
<body>
    <h1> Multimedia </h1>
    <audio controls>
        <source src="clip1.mpeg" type="audio/mpeg" />
    </audio>
    <br/>
    <video controls width="200" height="200">
        <source src="video1.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    </video>
</body>

​
Note:
  • width and height are for setting the dimensions for the video element
  • controls attribute creates buttons for playback (Play, Pause, etc.)
  • src (source) tag provides the source of the media file
  • type represents the type of the source file
Advantage : HTML was originally created for (hyper-)text documents, with perhaps a few images, not rich media pages with audio and video.  They required users to add special plugins like flash to their browsers. With audio and video tags, there is no dependency on external plugins.
Canvas element
The canvas tag in HTML5 helps users draw graphics or images on the fly using JavaScript. We can use it for drawing paths, boxes, circles, adding images, etc. The canvas tag has two attributes: width and height for setting the width and height of the canvas. Drawing on canvas is possible only by using javascript.
<html>
    <body>
        <canvas id="Canvas1" width="400" height="100" style="border:2px solid;">  
        </canvas>          
    </body>
</html>
New input types
input element in HTML, is reintroduced with new values like email, month, number, range, search, tel, color, week, url, time, date, datetime-local etc. These are the new values which can be given for type attribute of the input element. 
Validation attributes
HTML5 added new attributes that allows to set validation rules for a given input field. These new attributes include:
  • required: Specifies that the field can’t be blank
  • min/max: Specifies the range of allowed values for numeric inputs
  • minlength/maxlength: Specifies the range of allowed length for text inputs
  • step: For a step of n, a numeric input value is only valid if it is a multiple of n
  • pattern: Specifies a regular expression that a text input must match
Advantage : These attributes help in reducing java script coding for validation of data entered by user.

New attributes
  1. placeholder - It allows us to set placeholder text used for short descriptions. This text is deleted as soon as input gets focus.
  2. autofocus - Adding it to an input automatically focuses that field when the page is loaded in the browser.
  3. autocomplete - The autocomplete attribute helps users complete forms based on earlier input.
HTMLOutput
<form>
        <input type="text" name="username" placeholder="At least 3 characters"/> <br/>
        <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
    </form>		​
Once the cursor is in the text field
​
Attributes for input restrictions
 required -  the browser requires the user to enter data into that field before submitting the form. This replaces the basic form validation implemented with JavaScript
HTMLOutput
<form>
    User name : <br/>
    <input type="text" name="username" required/> <br/>
    User password : <br/>
    <input type="password" name="psw" /> <br/>
    <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
</form>		​

min, max and step
The min and max attributes specify the minimum and maximum values for an <input> element. The min and max attributes work with the following input types: number, range, date, datetime-local, month, time and week. The step attribute specifies the legal number intervals for an <input> element. Example: if step="3", legal numbers could be -3, 0, 3, 6, etc. The step attribute can be used together with the max and min attributes to create a range of legal values.
         Enter a date before 1980-01-01
        <input type="date" name="bday" max="1979-12-31"/> <br/>
       
        Enter a date after 2000-01-01
        <input type="date" name="bday" min="2000-01-02"/> <br/>
       
        Quantity (between 1 and 100)
        <input type="number" name="qty" min="1" max="100" step="5"/>

pattern
The pattern attribute specifies a regular expression that the <input> element's value is checked against. The pattern attribute works with the following input types: text, search, url, tel, email, and password.
         ​​​​​​​country code :
        <input type="text" name="ccode" pattern="[A-Za-z]{3}" title="three letter country code"
